hook: A $15 million satellite mission just went completely dark in orbit.

sections.voiceover: A $15 million satellite mission just went completely dark in orbit.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic shot of satellite silhouette drifting in deep space, Earth glowing below.
sections.sfx_cue: Low deep rumble fading into static.

sections.voiceover: Starfish Space launched the Otter 24C for the $15 million SSPICY technology demonstration mission. Its goal was inspecting inoperable satellites in low Earth orbit. Why did ground operators in Tukwila lose contact just one month after the November 2026 launch?
sections.visual_cue: Rocket launch footage transitioning to clean orbital trajectory map.
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle rocket roar followed by telemetry signal.
sections.animation_cue: Trajectory line arc across orbit diagram

sections.voiceover: But a fault protection system on the satellite blocked all communications with ground control teams.
sections.visual_cue: Schematic diagram of satellite internal systems highlighting fault sequence.
sections.sfx_cue: Sharp telemetry pulse fading to quiet static.
sections.animation_cue: Red alert outline pulse on telemetry graphic

sections.voiceover: NASA and Starfish Space concluded Otter 24C is not recoverable. The automated fault system permanently severed control from Tukwila. That failure ended the $15 million project prematurely.
sections.visual_cue: Wide dramatic view of Otter 24C floating unresponsive in dark orbit.
sections.animation_cue: Slow drift away from target satellite

sections.voiceover: Starfish Space lost its $15 million mission in low Earth orbit.
sections.visual_cue: Slow camera zoom out from Earth horizon into deep starfield.
b_roll: Low Earth orbit curvature photorealistic horizon
